strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: Clearly demonstrates and explains why temperature-based TTS fails for MDLMs (early stochastic errors propagate through iterative denoising), addressing a genuine gap in the literature

Comprehensive experimental validation: Evaluated on four benchmarks (LiveCodeBench, HumanEval+, MBPP+, MATH) with consistent improvements (e.g., 28% vs 21% on LiveCodeBench), extensive baseline comparisons (28 configurations including Best-of-N, DTS*, AB-MCTS), and thorough ablations

Sound technical approach: MCTS formulation appropriately applied with elegant caching mechanism enabling ~55% cache hit rate (7.69% performance gain at high NFE); clear algorithm design with practical considerations (tokenizer handling, special token mapping)

Strong empirical results with stable scaling: UMF shows 7-9 point improvements on coding benchmarks without performance fluctuations observed in stochastic baselines; demonstrates consistent gains across task types

Clear presentation and analysis: Well-written paper with effective visualizations (Figures 1, 4 showing search tree structure and collaborative generation); good case studies providing qualitative insights into model interaction patterns

Deterministic action design enables efficiency: The choice to use deterministic branching rather than stochastic sampling allows both high-quality trajectories and effective node caching, maximizing NFE utilization
weaknesses: Severely limited generality: Fundamental dependence on multiple pre-trained MDLMs restricts applicability. Evaluated only with two specific models (Dream-Coder, LLaDA); unclear how performance scales with 3+ models, weaker models, or different model pairs. Cannot be applied with single-model deployments—a critical limitation compared to DTS* and AB-MCTS which work single-model

Weak theoretical justification: Equation (1) is mathematically trivial (merely rearranges sums) and doesn't rigorously justify dynamic switching under exploration constraints. Section 5.2's variance argument is informal—conflates rollout variance with search process variance, contradicting the 'Var[R] ≈ 0' claim. No formal analysis of caching's sample efficiency contribution

Incomplete design justification: Mask ratio schedule [0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.4, 0.2] fixed without ablation; UCT exploration coefficient c_exp=1 not justified; fixed 768-token generation unmotivated; action space limited to 2 models without exploring temperature-based variants (Table 4 suggests hybrid approaches might help)

Incremental novelty: Core techniques exist in prior work (MCTS for diffusion in DTS/MEDAL, tree search in AB-MCTS). Primary novelty is treating models as discrete actions instead of stochastic perturbations—useful but somewhat incremental. Caching is natural optimization once deterministic actions introduced

Insufficient statistical rigor: Results appear single-seed without confidence intervals or significance tests despite small sample sizes (100 samples per benchmark). At NFE=12288, some improvements modest; MATH results notably weaker (~11 points) than coding (~28 points), limiting generalization claims

Fragile tokenizer handling: Text-based mapping strategy for non-special tokens lacks validation; no quantitative error analysis despite potential for silent corruption of code correctness. Only 6 tokenizer switches per 768-step generation appears risky for semantic preservation

Limited exploration of design space: No ablation on mask schedule, c_exp, generation length. Unclear how performance scales with >2 models or weaker model combinations. Missing comparison with simpler alternatives (e.g., sequential refinement with different models). Limited trajectory diversity analysis despite exploration claims

Experimental fairness concerns: UMF fundamentally uses multiple models by design while baselines often single-model or stochastic. Though AB-MCTS multi-model is included and beaten by UMF, comparison setup differs fundamentally. Most results at single NFE budget (12288); limited exploration of behavior at higher budgets

Reproducibility gaps: No code mentioned; missing implementation details (exact tie-breaking rules, tokenizer mapping edge cases, how private test cases generate rewards). Algorithm 1 line 12 (UnMaskToNextRatio) not formally defined regarding step count

Presentation and clarity issues: 'Remasking strategy' terminology confusing since unmasked tokens never re-masked; z subscript notation occasionally ambiguous; key details relegated to appendix; comparison with related work (DTS vs UMF differences) could be clearer

strengths: Well-motivated core insight distinguishing stochastic scaling effects on MDLMs vs. AR models, with clear intuition about error propagation through iterative refinement
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple benchmarks (LiveCodeBench, HumanEval+, MBPP+, MATH) with extensive baselines and ablations (28+ baseline configurations, Tables 3-5, 6-7)

Good experimental controls: Table 5 effectively demonstrates that interleaved multi-model unmasking (62.7%) outperforms independent single-model UMF pairs (57.0%), isolating the method's contribution from simple model aggregation

Technically solid algorithm design combining MCTS with deterministic rollout caching; practical implementation details well-addressed (tokenizer handling, block diffusion compatibility, runtime/memory analysis)
Clear presentation with precise algorithm description (Algorithm 1), effective visualizations of search trees and unmasking trajectories (Figures 3-4), and thorough appendix
weaknesses: Multi-model advantage not fully disentangled from MCTS benefits: main results (Table 1) compare multi-model UMF against single-model baselines; while Table 5 shows interleaving helps, head-to-head comparison with multi-model Best-of-N or DTS* at equal NFE would strengthen claims about the specific algorithmic contribution

Theoretical justification in Section 5 is incomplete: Equation (1) holds for any diverse kernels (not specific to deterministic multi-model branching); Section 5.2's Var[R]≈0 argument oversimplifies since different models produce different trajectory qualities independent of stochasticity—more rigorous formalization needed for why deterministic switching outperforms high-temperature sampling

Task-dependent improvements undermine 'consistent' performance claims: LiveCodeBench 47% relative improvement vs. MBPP+ 9% improvement; paper lacks analysis of what task characteristics determine UMF effectiveness

Severely limited evaluation scope: only coding and math benchmarks; no general language understanding, translation, or summarization tasks; small models (7-8B); unclear generalization to other MDLM families or larger scales

Practical deployment constraints insufficiently discussed: inference time ~700s per problem (Table 8), GPU memory 35.6GB for two models, makes real-world adoption questionable relative to speed/cost tradeoffs
